101def load_shared_module(name: str):
102 """!
103 @brief Load a module this file shares with the generators, such as `source_expressions`, from beside it.
104 @details A plain module rather than a package import, so this file works when it is loaded on
105 its own, as the tests do, and the generators load the same copy the same way.
106 @param[in] name Module name under `picurv_cli/`.
107 @return The module.
108 """
109 here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
110 if here not in sys.path:
111 sys.path.insert(0, here)
112 return importlib.import_module(name)
113

128def optional_matplotlib_pyplot():
129 """!
130 @brief Import matplotlib.pyplot lazily for study plot generation.
131 @return matplotlib.pyplot when available, otherwise None.
132 """
133 global _MATPLOTLIB_PYPLOT
134 if _MATPLOTLIB_PYPLOT is not None:
135 return _MATPLOTLIB_PYPLOT
136 original_path = list(sys.path)
137 try:
138 import matplotlib.pyplot as pyplot
139 except Exception:
140 try:
141 shared = load_shared_module("periodic_spectral")
142 shared.drop_imported_package("matplotlib")
143 sys.path = shared.prune_incompatible_python_site_paths(original_path)
144 import matplotlib.pyplot as pyplot
145 except Exception:
146 return None
147 finally:
148 sys.path = original_path
149 _MATPLOTLIB_PYPLOT = pyplot
150 return _MATPLOTLIB_PYPLOT

177def _read_release_version() -> str:
178 """!
179 @brief Read the single release version shared by every PICurv executable.
180 @return Release version from VERSION, or a safe development fallback.

183 if configured:

◆ _source_build_identity()

dict picurv_cli.core._source_build_identity ( str  release_version)
protected

Resolve reproducible release, commit, and dirty-tree build identity.

One git describe --long --dirty gives the commit, its distance from the release tag, and whether tracked files differ from it (untracked files are ignored, as git status --untracked-files=no did). Only when the tag is missing does it fall back to the commit, a dirty check, and the commit count. On a cold network filesystem each git call costs seconds, which is why this is reached lazily through picurv_build() rather than at import.

Parameters
[in]release_versionRelease version read from VERSION.
Returns
Mapping suitable for manifests and user-facing status output.

210 @details One `git describe --long --dirty` gives the commit, its distance from the
211 release tag, and whether tracked files differ from it (untracked files are
212 ignored, as `git status --untracked-files=no` did). Only when the tag is
213 missing does it fall back to the commit, a dirty check, and the commit count.
214 On a cold network filesystem each git call costs seconds, which is why this is
215 reached lazily through picurv_build() rather than at import.
216 @param[in] release_version Release version read from VERSION.
217 @return Mapping suitable for manifests and user-facing status output.
218 """
219 identity = {
220 "release_version": release_version,
221 "version": release_version,
222 "git_commit": None,
223 "git_short_commit": None,
224 "dirty": None,
225 "build_id": release_version,
226 "dev_distance": None,
227 "released": False,
228 }
229 described = _git_output("describe", "--tags", "--long", "--dirty", "--abbrev=40",
230 "--match", f"v{release_version}")
231 match = re.match(r"^v.+-(\d+)-g([0-9a-f]{40})(-dirty)?$", described or "")
232 if match:
233 identity["dev_distance"] = int(match.group(1))
234 identity["git_commit"] = match.group(2)
235 identity["dirty"] = bool(match.group(3))
236 else:
237 # No tag for this release yet: every commit is development toward it.
238 identity["git_commit"] = _git_output("rev-parse", "HEAD")
239 status = _git_output("status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=no")
240 identity["dirty"] = None if status is None else bool(status)
241 count = _git_output("rev-list", "--count", "HEAD")
242 if count is not None and count.isdigit():
243 identity["dev_distance"] = int(count)
244 if identity["git_commit"]:
245 identity["git_short_commit"] = identity["git_commit"][:12]
246 # Commits since the release tag, so a development build is visibly ahead of the
247 # release it names rather than claiming to be that release.
248 identity["released"] = identity["dev_distance"] == 0 and not identity["dirty"]
249 if identity["git_short_commit"]:
250 development = "" if identity["dev_distance"] in (0, None) else f".dev{identity['dev_distance']}"
251 suffix = f"{development}+g{identity['git_short_commit']}"
252 if identity["dirty"]:
253 suffix += ".dirty"
254 identity["build_id"] = release_version + suffix
255 identity["version"] = identity["build_id"]
256 return identity

439 @brief Find a named file at or above an arbitrary filesystem anchor.
440 @param[in] start File or directory from which to search.
441 @param[in] filename Basename to locate.
442 @return Absolute path when found, otherwise None.
443 """
444 current = os.path.abspath(start or os.getcwd())

452 if parent == current:
453 return None

530def enforce_reproducibility_policy(workspace_root: str) -> dict:
531 """!
532 @brief Enforce an optional workspace policy demanding a clean, released build.
533
534 @details Exploratory work should stay frictionless, so this is opt-in: a workspace
535 running a campaign that will be published sets it once, and PICurv then
536 refuses to stage from a modified or untagged tree instead of recording the
537 compromise in a manifest nobody reads until later.
538 @param[in] workspace_root Initialized workspace directory, or None.
539 @return The resolved policy mapping, empty when none is configured.
540 @throws ValueError when the active build does not satisfy the configured policy.
541 """
542 if not workspace_root:
543 return {}
544 payload = load_workspace_config(workspace_root)
545 policy = payload.get("reproducibility") or {}
546 if not isinstance(policy, dict) or not policy:
547 return {}
548 if policy.get("require_clean_release"):
549 problems = []
550 if picurv_build().get("dirty"):
551 problems.append("the source tree has uncommitted changes")
552 if picurv_build().get("dev_distance"):
553 problems.append(
554 f"HEAD is {picurv_build()['dev_distance']} commit(s) past the "
555 f"v{PICURV_RELEASE_VERSION} release tag"
556 )
557 elif picurv_build().get("dev_distance") is None:
558 problems.append("the release tag could not be resolved from this checkout")
559 if problems:
560 raise ValueError(
561 f"{WORKSPACE_CONFIG_FILENAME} sets reproducibility.require_clean_release, "
562 f"but this build is {picurv_build()['build_id']}: " + "; ".join(problems) + ".\n"
563 "Commit and tag the release, or clear the policy for exploratory work."
564 )
565 if policy.get("pin_executables"):
566 identities = runtime_build_identities()
567 stale = [
568 name for name, identity in sorted(identities.items())
569 if identity.get("available") and not identity.get("matches_source")
570 ]
571 unavailable = [
572 name for name, identity in sorted(identities.items())
573 if not identity.get("available")
574 ]
575 if stale or unavailable:
576 detail = []
577 if stale:
578 detail.append("built from another revision: " + ", ".join(stale))
579 if unavailable:
580 detail.append("no build identity available: " + ", ".join(unavailable))
581 commands = sorted({rebuild_command(name, identities[name]) for name in stale + unavailable})
582 raise ValueError(
583 f"{WORKSPACE_CONFIG_FILENAME} sets reproducibility.pin_executables, but "
584 "the executables do not match the active source (" + "; ".join(detail) + ").\n"
585 "Rebuild with " + " and ".join(f"'{command}'" for command in commands)
586 + " so the run records the build that produced it."
587 )
588 return dict(policy)

591def resolve_workspace_path(anchor_file: str, candidate: str, *, allow_external: bool = False) -> str:
592 """!
593 @brief Resolve a user path against its workspace and reject implicit escapes.
594 @param[in] anchor_file Config file whose workspace owns the reference.
595 @param[in] candidate Workspace-relative path text.
596 @param[in] allow_external Whether an explicit import/reference operation permits an absolute path.
597 @return Absolute resolved path.
598 """
599 if not isinstance(candidate, str) or not candidate.strip():
600 raise ValueError("Referenced path must be a non-empty string.")
601 text = os.path.expanduser(candidate.strip())
602 workspace_root = find_workspace_root(anchor_file)
603 if not workspace_root:
604 return os.path.abspath(text if os.path.isabs(text) else os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(anchor_file)), text))
605 if os.path.isabs(text):
606 if allow_external:
607 return os.path.abspath(text)
608 raise ValueError(
609 f"{anchor_file}: absolute path {candidate!r} is not allowed in workspace configuration; "
610 "import it with 'picurv inputs import' or use an explicit reference-mode import."
611 )
612 resolved = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(workspace_root, text))
613 if os.path.commonpath([workspace_root, resolved]) != os.path.abspath(workspace_root):
614 raise ValueError(
615 f"{anchor_file}: path {candidate!r} escapes the workspace; parent traversal is not allowed."
616 )
617 if resolved.endswith(".reference.yml") and os.path.isfile(resolved):
618 pointer = read_yaml_file(resolved)
619 external = pointer.get("picurv_external_reference") if isinstance(pointer, dict) else None
620 if not isinstance(external, str) or not os.path.isabs(external):
621 raise ValueError(f"Invalid external-reference descriptor: {resolved}")
622 if not os.path.isfile(external):
623 raise ValueError(f"Registered external input is unavailable: {external}")
624 return external
625 return resolved

tuple picurv_cli.core.validate_run_directory_structure ( str  run_dir)

Refuse a run whose root has grown a directory the layout does not define.

The run topology is a contract: manifest.json publishes it, the solver's reserved-directory guard defends it, and storage classifies against it. A directory beside output/ breaks all three at once - it is routed by nothing, classified as unclassified, and therefore archived forever and pruned never. Catching it when the run is staged or resumed is the only point where the answer is still "move it", rather than "it is already in every archive of this run".

Unexpected files are reported and allowed. A stray note at a run root costs nothing and refusing to resume a long campaign over one would be a worse failure than the one being prevented.

686def validate_run_directory_structure(run_dir: str) -> tuple:
687 """!
688 @brief Refuse a run whose root has grown a directory the layout does not define.
689
690 @details The run topology is a contract: `manifest.json` publishes it, the solver's
691 reserved-directory guard defends it, and storage classifies against it. A
692 directory beside `output/` breaks all three at once - it is routed by
693 nothing, classified as `unclassified`, and therefore archived forever and
694 pruned never. Catching it when the run is staged or resumed is the only
695 point where the answer is still "move it", rather than "it is already in
696 every archive of this run".
697
698 Unexpected *files* are reported and allowed. A stray note at a run root
699 costs nothing and refusing to resume a long campaign over one would be a
700 worse failure than the one being prevented.
701 @param[in] run_dir Run root to check.
702 @return Tuple of (errors, warnings) as human-readable message lists.
703 """
704 root = os.path.abspath(run_dir)
705 if not os.path.isdir(root):
706 return [], []
707 allowed_files = set(RUN_ROOT_ALLOWED_FILES) | {
708 STORAGE_STATE_FILENAME, STORAGE_LOCK_FILENAME,
709 }
710 errors, warnings = [], []
711 for name in sorted(os.listdir(root)):
712 path = os.path.join(root, name)
713 if os.path.isdir(path) and not os.path.islink(path):
714 if name not in RUN_DIRECTORY_ROOTS:
715 errors.append(
716 f"{run_dir}: '{name}/' is not part of the run layout. Scientific "
717 f"output belongs under {CANONICAL_RUN_PATHS['checkpoints']}, "
718 f"{CANONICAL_RUN_PATHS['analysis']}, or "
719 f"{CANONICAL_RUN_PATHS['visualization']}; move or remove '{name}/' "
720 f"before running. Run-owned roots are: "
721 + ", ".join(sorted(RUN_DIRECTORY_ROOTS)) + "."
722 )
723 elif name not in allowed_files:
724 warnings.append(
725 f"{run_dir}: unexpected file '{name}' at the run root. It is archived "
726 "as unclassified and never pruned."
727 )
728 return errors, warnings

771def allocate_generated_run_id(runs_root: str, case_cfg: dict, case_path: str) -> str:
772 """!
773 @brief Build the generated run identity, disambiguating a same-second collision.
774
775 @details The identity is `<run label>_<timestamp>` at one-second resolution, so two
776 runs of the same case launched back to back - a script, or a smoke
777 sequence - would otherwise name the same directory. Creating a run never
778 writes into an existing one, so the identity is advanced instead of the
779 launch being refused for a clock artifact.
780 @param[in] runs_root Directory generated runs are created beneath.
781 @param[in] case_cfg Parsed case configuration supplying the run label.
782 @param[in] case_path Case path, for the label's fallback.
783 @return Run identity that does not currently exist under `runs_root`.
784 """
785 base = f"{case_run_label(case_cfg, case_path)}_{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S')}"

787 while os.path.exists(os.path.join(runs_root, run_id)):
788 suffix += 1
789 run_id = f"{base}-{suffix}"
790 return run_id

793def discard_unused_run_directory(run_dir: str, *, created: bool, staged: bool = False) -> bool:
794 """!
795 @brief Remove a generated run directory that never received any content.
796
797 @details Only a directory this invocation created, and which still holds no files,
798 is removed: an existing run, or one that already produced output, is never
799 touched by a staging failure. With @p staged the directory may hold the files
800 this invocation staged, for a refusal after staging but before any launch.
801 @param[in] run_dir Run directory that was about to be staged.
802 @param[in] created Whether this invocation created the directory.
803 @param[in] staged Whether files this invocation staged, and nothing else, may be present.
804 @return True when the directory was removed.
805 """
806 if not created or not os.path.isdir(run_dir):
807 return False
808 for _root, _dirs, files in os.walk(run_dir):
809 if files and not staged:
810 return False

878def _toolchain_identity() -> dict:
879 """!
880 @brief Best-effort record of the PETSc, MPI, and compiler in the shell staging the run.
881 @details This is the staging environment, which need not be what the binaries were
882 built against; each executable's own PETSc is recorded from its build stamp.
883 @return Mapping of what could be determined; absent keys mean it could not be read.
884 """
885 identity = {}
886 petsc_dir = os.environ.get("PETSC_DIR")
887 if petsc_dir:
888 identity["petsc_dir"] = petsc_dir
889 version_header = os.path.join(petsc_dir, "include", "petscversion.h")
890 try:
891 with open(version_header, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as stream:
892 numbers = {}
893 for line in stream:
894 match = re.match(
895 r"#define\s+PETSC_VERSION_(MAJOR|MINOR|SUBMINOR)\s+(\d+)", line
896 )
897 if match:
898 numbers[match.group(1)] = match.group(2)
899 if len(numbers) == 3:
900 identity["petsc_version"] = (
901 f"{numbers['MAJOR']}.{numbers['MINOR']}.{numbers['SUBMINOR']}"
902 )
903 except OSError:
904 pass
905 if os.environ.get("PETSC_ARCH"):
906 identity["petsc_arch"] = os.environ["PETSC_ARCH"]
907 for tool, key in (("mpiexec", "mpi"), ("mpicc", "compiler")):
908 executable = shutil.which(tool)
909 if not executable:
910 continue
911 try:
912 result = subprocess.run(
913 [executable, "--version"], text=True, capture_output=True, timeout=20, check=False
914 )
915 except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
916 continue
917 first = (result.stdout or result.stderr or "").strip().splitlines()
918 if first:
919 identity[key] = first[0][:200]
920 return identity

1469def _recorded_run_root(run_dir: str):
1470 """!
1471 @brief Return the location a run's generated files refer to.
1472 @details Runs staged before the manifest recorded `root_path` are read from the
1473 active control file, whose generated input paths all start at the run root.

1479 return manifest["root_path"]

1482 return None

1484 with open(control, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as stream:
1485 for line in stream:
1486 for token in line.split()[1:]:
1487 for marker in markers:
1488 if not (token.startswith("/") and marker in token):
1489 continue
1490 candidate, rest = token.split(marker, 1)
1491 # Only a path that names a file of this run identifies its old root;
1492 # an external input that merely contains the same segment does not.
1493 if os.path.exists(os.path.join(run_dir, marker.strip("/"), rest)):
1494 return candidate
1495 return None

1860def read_binary_petsc_stamp(executable_path: str) -> "dict | None":
1861 """!
1862 @brief Read the PETSc build stamp from an executable's bytes, without running it.
1863 @details A binary built against one PETSc and started against another cannot run
1864 `--version` at all, which is exactly when knowing its PETSc matters.
1865 @param[in] executable_path Path to `simulator` or `postprocessor`.
1866 @return The parsed stamp, or None when the file carries none (built before it existed).

1870 data = stream.read()

1875 return None
1876 start += len(_BINARY_PETSC_STAMP_MARKER)

1878 return _parse_binary_petsc_line(text.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"))

1928def _read_binary_build_stamp(executable_path: str) -> "dict | None":
1929 """!
1930 @brief Read the build identity stamped into an executable's bytes, without running it.
1931 @details src/setup.c stores `PICURV_BUILD:<version> <commit> <dirty>` beside the PETSc
1932 stamp. Running `--version` on a login node starts the dynamic loader against a
1933 cold filesystem, tens of seconds; reading the file costs one read.
1934 @param[in] executable_path Path to `simulator` or `postprocessor`.
1935 @return The identity mapping `read_binary_build_identity()` returns, or None for a binary
1936 built before the stamp existed.
1937 """
1938 try:
1939 with open(executable_path, "rb") as stream:
1940 data = stream.read()
1941 except OSError:
1942 return None
1943 start = data.find(_BINARY_BUILD_STAMP_MARKER)
1944 if start < 0:
1945 return None
1946 fields = data[start + len(_BINARY_BUILD_STAMP_MARKER):start + 512].split(b"\0", 1)[0].decode(
1947 "utf-8", errors="replace").split()
1948 if len(fields) != 3 or not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]+", fields[1]) or fields[2] not in ("true", "false"):
1949 return None

1951 release = re.sub(r"\.dev\d+$", "", version)
1952 petsc = read_binary_petsc_stamp(executable_path)
1953 if petsc is None:
1954 return None
1955 # Exactly what `--version` prints (src/setup.c), which the job-start check compares with.
1956 name = os.path.basename(executable_path)
1957 version_line = (f"{name} {version}+g{commit}{'.dirty' if dirty else ''}\n"
1958 f"petsc {petsc['version']} {petsc['mode']}"
1959 f"{' ' + petsc['indices'] if petsc.get('indices_stamped') else ''} {petsc['arch']} {petsc['dir']}")

1961 "available": True,
1962 "path": executable_path,
1963 "version_line": version_line,
1964 "release_version": release,
1965 "git_commit": commit,
1966 "dirty": dirty,
1967 "build_id": f"{version}+g{commit}{'.dirty' if dirty else ''}",
1968 "petsc": petsc,
1969 "identity_source": "stamp",

1973def read_binary_build_identity(executable_path: str) -> dict:
1974 """!
1975 @brief Read the build identity a native executable was compiled with.
1976
1977 @details The Makefile stamps the release, commit, and dirty state into the
1978 binaries, and they are written into every checkpoint manifest. Reading it
1979 back is what makes the run manifest's provenance a statement about the
1980 binary that ran rather than about whatever source happens to be checked
1981 out when the conductor is invoked.
1982 @param[in] executable_path Path to `simulator` or `postprocessor`.
1983 @return Identity mapping, or an `available: False` mapping when it cannot be read.
1984 """
1985 if not os.path.isfile(executable_path) or not os.access(executable_path, os.X_OK):
1986 return {"available": False, "reason": "not built", "path": executable_path}
1987 stamped = _read_binary_build_stamp(executable_path)
1988 if stamped is not None:
1989 return stamped
1990 try:
1991 result = subprocess.run(
1992 [executable_path, "--version"], text=True, capture_output=True, timeout=30,
1993 )
1994 except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as exc:
1995 return {"available": False, "reason": str(exc), "path": executable_path}
1996 if result.returncode != 0:
1997 # A binary that cannot start - typically its shared libraries are not loadable
1998 # in this shell - is not the same failure as one that predates the identity
1999 # flag, and recording it as such hides a broken staging environment.
2000 detail = (result.stderr or result.stdout or "").strip().splitlines()
2001 return {"available": False,
2002 "reason": f"--version exited {result.returncode}"
2003 + (f": {detail[0]}" if detail else ""),
2004 "path": executable_path,
2005 "petsc": read_binary_petsc_stamp(executable_path)}
2006 lines = (result.stdout or "").strip().splitlines()
2007 match = _BINARY_VERSION_PATTERN.match(lines[0] if lines else "")
2008 if not match:
2009 # A binary from before the identity flag existed, or a wrapper that prints
2010 # something else. Recorded as unavailable rather than guessed at.
2011 return {"available": False, "reason": "no build identity reported",
2012 "path": executable_path}
2013 return {
2014 "available": True,
2015 "path": executable_path,
2016 "version_line": (result.stdout or "").strip(),
2017 "release_version": match.group("release"),
2018 "git_commit": match.group("commit"),
2019 "dirty": bool(match.group("dirty")),
2020 "build_id": (
2021 f"{match.group('version')}+g{match.group('commit')}"
2022 f"{'.dirty' if match.group('dirty') else ''}"
2023 ),
2024 "petsc": _parse_binary_petsc_line(lines[1]) if len(lines) > 1 else None,
2025 }

3640 @brief Resolve the scalar-transport parameters from case.yml or their deprecated location.
3641 @details Each parameter is read from its case.yml location (SCALAR_TRANSPORT_CASE_PATHS)

3653 unknown = sorted(set(legacy) - set(SCALAR_TRANSPORT_FLAGS))
3654 if unknown:
3655 raise ValueError(f"solver.yml scalar_transport has unsupported key(s): {unknown}. "
3656 f"Use one of {sorted(SCALAR_TRANSPORT_FLAGS)}, in case.yml.")

3664 if in_case and key in legacy:
3665 raise ValueError(f"{key} is set in case.yml ({case_label}) and in its deprecated "
3666 f"solver.yml location (scalar_transport.{key}); keep only the case.yml one.")

3670 (legacy[key], f"solver.yml scalar_transport.{key}")

3674 else:
3675 value = _to_float(raw, label)

3677 raise ValueError(f"{label} must be positive.")
3678 if not in_case and warn:
3679 print(f"[WARNING] solver.yml scalar_transport.{key} is deprecated; set it in case.yml "
3680 f"as {case_label}.", file=sys.stderr)

3741def normalize_post_spectra_config(post_cfg: dict) -> dict:
3742 """!
3743 @brief Validate and canonicalize the spectra block of post.yml.
3744
3745 @details The recipe chooses what to measure; whether the case *can* support that
3746 measurement is a separate question answered by
3747 `validate_post_spectra_preconditions()`, which needs the grid and the
3748 boundary conditions. Keeping the two apart means a recipe stays valid on
3749 its own terms even when it is read without a case beside it.
3750
3751 @param[in] post_cfg Parsed post-processing configuration.
3752 @return Normalized mapping with an output prefix and a list of tasks.
3753 @throws ValueError on a malformed or inconsistent recipe.
3754 """
3755 raw = (post_cfg or {}).get("spectra")
3756 if raw is None:
3757 return {"output_prefix": "Spectrum", "tasks": []}
3758 if not isinstance(raw, dict):
3759 raise ValueError("'spectra' must be a mapping.")
3760
3761 prefix = raw.get("output_prefix", "Spectrum")
3762 if not isinstance(prefix, str) or not prefix.strip():
3763 raise ValueError("'spectra.output_prefix' must be a non-empty string.")
3764

3767 raise ValueError("'spectra.tasks' must be a non-empty list.")
3768

3771 for position, entry in enumerate(tasks):
3772 if not isinstance(entry, dict):
3773 raise ValueError(f"spectra task {position}: each task must be a mapping.")
3774 name = entry.get("task")
3775 if not isinstance(name, str) or name not in POST_SPECTRA_TASKS:
3776 raise ValueError(
3777 f"spectra task {position}: unknown task {name!r}. "
3778 f"Available tasks: {sorted(POST_SPECTRA_TASKS)}."
3779 )
3780 spec = POST_SPECTRA_TASKS[name]
3781
3782 field = entry.get("field", spec["fields"][0])
3783 if field not in spec["fields"]:
3784 raise ValueError(
3785 f"spectra task '{name}': field {field!r} is not supported. "
3786 f"Supported fields: {list(spec['fields'])}."
3787 )
3788
3789 block = entry.get("block", 0)
3790 if not isinstance(block, int) or isinstance(block, bool) or block < 0:
3791 raise ValueError(f"spectra task '{name}': 'block' must be a non-negative integer.")
3792
3793 symbol = entry.get("symbol", "continuum")
3794 if symbol not in POST_SPECTRA_SYMBOLS:
3795 raise ValueError(
3796 f"spectra task '{name}': unknown symbol {symbol!r}. "
3797 f"Available symbols: {list(POST_SPECTRA_SYMBOLS)}."
3798 )
3799
3800 subtract_mean = entry.get("subtract_mean", "none")
3801 if not isinstance(subtract_mean, str) or not subtract_mean.strip():
3802 raise ValueError(f"spectra task '{name}': 'subtract_mean' must be a string.")
3803 subtract_mean = subtract_mean.strip()
3804 if subtract_mean.startswith("window:"):
3805 window_name = subtract_mean.split(":", 1)[1].strip()
3806 if not window_name:
3807 raise ValueError(
3808 f"spectra task '{name}': 'subtract_mean: window:<name>' needs a window name."
3809 )
3810 elif subtract_mean not in POST_SPECTRA_MEAN_MODES:
3811 raise ValueError(
3812 f"spectra task '{name}': unknown subtract_mean {subtract_mean!r}. "
3813 f"Use one of {list(POST_SPECTRA_MEAN_MODES)} or 'window:<name>'."
3814 )
3815
3816 # A window mean is only worth subtracting once the window has converged, so the
3817 # bundle the mean is read from is chosen separately from the step being
3818 # transformed. Left unset, each step uses its own bundle, whose running mean is
3819 # undefined at the moment the window activates.
3820 mean_source_step = entry.get("mean_source_step")
3821 if mean_source_step is not None:
3822 if (not isinstance(mean_source_step, int) or isinstance(mean_source_step, bool)
3823 or mean_source_step < 0):
3824 raise ValueError(
3825 f"spectra task '{name}': 'mean_source_step' must be a non-negative integer."
3826 )
3827 if not subtract_mean.startswith("window:"):
3828 raise ValueError(
3829 f"spectra task '{name}': 'mean_source_step' only applies to "
3830 f"'subtract_mean: window:<name>'."
3831 )
3832

3834 if reference is not None and (not isinstance(reference, str) or not reference.strip()):
3835 raise ValueError(f"spectra task '{name}': 'reference' must be a non-empty string.")
3836

3839 axes = entry.get("axes")
3840 fixed = entry.get("fixed_indices")
3841 count = 2 if name == "plane_spectrum" else 1
3842 if (not isinstance(axes, list) or len(axes) != count or any(a not in ("i", "j", "k") for a in axes)

3854 if identity in seen:

3857 f"with symbol '{symbol}' more than once."

3863 "field": field,

3867 "mean_source_step": mean_source_step,

Measure spectra for every requested task across a window of committed steps.

One spectrum per step per task, because a spectrum is a property of one state: averaging across steps would be wrong for a decaying flow, where every step is a different statistical state. Results are written in long form so a family of curves stays one file, alongside a scalar history that plots through the ordinary series machinery.

4234def normalize_post_reducers_config(post_cfg: dict) -> dict:
4235 """!
4236 @brief Validate and canonicalize the reducers block of post.yml.
4237 @details A reducer reads the profiles `field_statistics` writes, so each task names a
4238 window or ensemble of the same recipe, and the recipe's `homogeneous` must
4239 leave the directions the task needs.
4240 @param[in] post_cfg Parsed post-processing configuration.
4241 @return Mapping with the canonical task list.
4242 """
4243 raw = (post_cfg or {}).get("reducers")
4244 if raw is None:
4245 return {"tasks": []}
4246 if not isinstance(raw, dict) or not isinstance(raw.get("tasks"), list) or not raw["tasks"]:
4247 raise ValueError("'reducers' must be a mapping with a non-empty 'tasks' list.")
4248 statistics = normalize_post_field_statistics_config(post_cfg)
4249 windows = set(statistics["windows"])
4250 owners = windows | {ensemble["name"] for ensemble in statistics["ensembles"]}
4251 retained = [axis for axis in ("i", "j", "k") if axis not in statistics["homogeneous"]]
4252 tasks = []
4253 for index, entry in enumerate(raw["tasks"]):
4254 if not isinstance(entry, dict):
4255 raise ValueError(f"'reducers.tasks[{index}]' must be a mapping.")
4256 name = entry.get("task")
4257 if not isinstance(name, str) or name not in POST_REDUCER_TASKS:
4258 raise ValueError(f"reducer task {name!r} is unknown. Available tasks: {sorted(POST_REDUCER_TASKS)}.")
4259 spec = POST_REDUCER_TASKS[name]
4260 label = f"reducer '{name}'"
4261 source = entry.get("source")
4262 if not isinstance(source, str) or source not in owners:
4263 raise ValueError(f"{label}: 'source' must name a field_statistics window or ensemble of this "
4264 f"recipe (got {source!r}; available: {sorted(owners)}).")
4265 if "csv" not in statistics["formats"] or len(retained) != spec["retains"]:
4266 raise ValueError(f"{label} reads a profile keeping {spec['retains']} direction(s), so "
4267 f"field_statistics needs 'csv' in formats and 'homogeneous' leaving that "
4268 f"many (it leaves {retained}).")
4269 task = {"task": name, "source": source}
4270 if spec["axis_key"]:
4271 axis = entry.get(spec["axis_key"], spec["default_axis"])
4272 if axis not in _REDUCER_AXIS_TOKENS:
4273 raise ValueError(f"{label}: '{spec['axis_key']}' must be one of i, j, k (got {axis!r}).")
4274 kept = axis in retained
4275 if kept != (spec["axis_key"] == "wall_axis"):
4276 raise ValueError(f"{label}: the profile {'must keep' if not kept else 'must merge over'} "
4277 f"'{axis}', but 'homogeneous' is {statistics['homogeneous']}.")
4278 task[spec["axis_key"]] = axis
4279 stream = entry.get("stream_axis", "k")
4280 if stream not in _REDUCER_AXIS_TOKENS or stream == task.get("wall_axis"):
4281 raise ValueError(f"{label}: 'stream_axis' must be i, j or k and differ from the wall axis.")
4282 task["stream_axis"] = stream
4283 friction = entry.get("friction_velocity", "first_cell")
4284 if friction not in POST_REDUCER_FRICTION_SOURCES or (name == "cross_section" and friction == "wall_model"):
4285 raise ValueError(f"{label}: 'friction_velocity' must be one of "
4286 f"{[f for f in POST_REDUCER_FRICTION_SOURCES if name != 'cross_section' or f != 'wall_model']} "
4287 f"(got {friction!r}).")
4288 needs = POST_REDUCER_FRICTION_SOURCES.get(friction, {}).get("needs")
4289 if needs == "window" and source not in windows:
4290 raise ValueError(f"{label}: friction_velocity '{friction}' averages over a run window's time "
4291 f"bounds, so 'source' must be a run window, not an ensemble.")
4292 task["friction_velocity"] = friction
4293 if needs == "value":
4294 task["value"] = _to_finite_float(entry.get("value"), f"reducers.tasks[{index}].value",
4295 positive=True, strict=True)
4296 if name == "cross_section":
4297 task["fold"] = _to_bool(entry.get("fold", True), f"reducers.tasks[{index}].fold")
4298 if name == "wall_profile" and entry.get("half_height") is not None:
4299 task["half_height"] = _to_finite_float(entry["half_height"], f"reducers.tasks[{index}].half_height",
4300 positive=True)
4301 tasks.append(task)

4306 """!
4307 @brief Run every reducer task over the profiles the recipe has written.
4308 @details Reducers read only small CSVs, so every profile present is reduced again on
4309 each invocation rather than tracked step by step. Inputs come from the run:
4310 the viscosity and reference scales from its case snapshot, the grid it was

4413def _merge_spectra_rows(path: str, fieldnames: tuple, remeasured: set, new_rows: list) -> list:
4414 """!
4415 @brief Combine newly measured spectra rows with those already written for other steps.
4416 @details The file belongs to one recipe, whose identity covers the spectra settings, so
4417 its existing rows come from the same measurement. Rows for a re-measured step
4418 are replaced; rows for every other step are kept. A file whose columns differ
4419 is not merged: it was written by another format and is rewritten whole.
4420 @param[in] path Existing CSV path, which may be absent.
4421 @param[in] fieldnames Columns the new rows carry.
4422 @param[in] remeasured Steps measured in this invocation.
4423 @param[in] new_rows Rows measured in this invocation.
4424 @return All rows, ordered by step with each step's rows in their measured order.
4425 """
4426 kept = []
4427 try:
4428 with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
4429 reader = csv.DictReader(stream)
4430 if tuple(reader.fieldnames or ()) == tuple(fieldnames):
4431 kept = [row for row in reader if int(row["step"]) not in remeasured]
4432 except FileNotFoundError:
4433 pass
4434 return sorted(kept + list(new_rows), key=lambda row: int(row["step"]))

4437def compute_post_spectra_signature(spectra_cfg: dict) -> str:

4638def _post_window_derived_field_count(window_cfg: dict, outputs: list, eligible: dict = None) -> int:
4639 """!
4640 @brief Count the derived fields one window would produce for a set of outputs.
4641
4642 @details Mirrors the resolution the C derivation performs, so a recipe that would
4643 produce an empty file is refused before the run rather than after it. Each
4644 output resolves against what the window accumulated: a window keeping only
4645 first moments has no stresses, RMS, or turbulent kinetic energy to give.
4646
4647 @param[in] window_cfg Normalized window definition from monitor.yml.
4648 @param[in] outputs Requested output kinds.
4649 @param[in] eligible Field table the window's fields are named from; the Eulerian
4650 table when None.
4651 @return Value returned by `_post_window_derived_field_count()`.
4652 """
4653 eligible = STATISTICS_ELIGIBLE_FIELDS if eligible is None else eligible
4654 fields = window_cfg.get("fields", []) or []
4655 covariances = window_cfg.get("covariances", []) or []
4656 with_second = [f for f in fields if "second" in (f.get("moments") or [])]
4657 total = 0
4658 for kind in outputs:
4659 if kind == "mean":
4660 total += len(fields)
4661 elif kind == "reynolds_stress":
4662 for entry in with_second:
4663 dof = eligible[entry["field"]]["components"]
4664 total += 6 if dof == 3 else 1
4665 elif kind == "rms":
4666 for entry in with_second:
4667 total += eligible[entry["field"]]["components"]
4668 elif kind == "tke":
4669 total += sum(1 for entry in with_second
4670 if eligible[entry["field"]]["components"] == 3)
4671 elif kind == "flux":
4672 total += len(covariances)
4673 return total

4690def get_post_field_statistics_artifacts(post_cfg: dict, run_dir: str):
4691 """!
4692 @brief Predict the per-window statistics artifacts a recipe will produce.
4693 @details Returns one entry per window and format, so resume tracking can tell a
4694 half-finished window from a completed one.
4695 @param[in] post_cfg Parsed post-processing configuration.
4696 @param[in] run_dir Run directory the outputs are written under.
4697 @return List of (kind, path_prefix, window) tuples; kind is 'vtk', 'csv' (a history
4698 shared by every step) or 'profile' (a prefix taking `_<step>.csv`). window is
4699 None for a recipe ensemble, which every processed step produces.
4700 """
4701 config = normalize_post_field_statistics_config(post_cfg)
4702 if not (config["windows"] or config["ensembles"]):
4703 return []
4704 io_cfg = post_cfg.get("io", {}) or {}
4705 internal = (post_cfg or {}).get("_picurv_paths", {}) or {}
4706 visualization_dir = _post_output_directory_abs(run_dir, post_cfg)
4707 visualization_prefix = io_cfg.get("output_filename_prefix", "Field")
4708 csv_prefix_path = None
4709 if internal.get("field_statistics_prefix"):
4710 csv_prefix_path = os.path.join(run_dir, internal["field_statistics_prefix"])
4711 csv_base = csv_prefix_path or os.path.join(visualization_dir, str(visualization_prefix))
4712 artifacts = []
4713 # An ensemble is built from the step itself, so every processed step produces it;
4714 # its entries carry no window, which marks them as always expected.
4715 owners = [(window, window) for window in config["windows"]]
4716 owners += [(ensemble["name"], None) for ensemble in config["ensembles"]]
4717 for name, window in owners:
4718 if "vtk" in config["formats"]:
4719 artifacts.append(("vtk", os.path.join(
4720 visualization_dir, f"{visualization_prefix}_statistics_{name}"
4721 ), window))
4722 if "csv" in config["formats"] and window is not None:
4723 artifacts.append(("csv", f"{csv_base}_statistics_{name}.csv", window))
4724 if "csv" in config["formats"] and config["homogeneous"]:
4725 artifacts.append(("profile", f"{csv_base}_profile_{name}", window))
4726 return artifacts
4727

4857def compute_post_recipe_id(post_cfg: dict) -> str:
4858 """!
4859 @brief Compute a stable human-readable identity for one post recipe.
4860 @param[in] post_cfg Parsed post configuration before runtime path injection.
4861 @return Filesystem-safe recipe identity.
4862 """
4863 normalized = copy.deepcopy(post_cfg or {})
4864 normalized.pop("_picurv_paths", None)
4865 # source_data.directory is always replaced by the run's own output, so an absent
4866 # block and an emptied one are the same recipe; both hash as the emptied form that
4867 # every earlier recipe, which carried the directory, reduced to.
4868 source = normalized.setdefault("source_data", {})
4869 if isinstance(source, dict):
4870 source.pop("directory", None)
4871 io = normalized.get("io")
4872 label = "post"
4873 if isinstance(io, dict):
4874 io.pop("output_directory", None)
4875 # ParaView collection generation changes only how existing VTK artifacts are
4876 # indexed. It must not split an otherwise identical computational recipe,
4877 # especially when a child enables lineage indexing for an ancestor whose VTK
4878 # files predate the option.
4879 io.pop("paraview_series", None)
4880 raw_label = io.get("output_filename_prefix")
4881 if isinstance(raw_label, str) and raw_label.strip():
4882 label = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]+", "-", raw_label.strip()).strip("-") or "post"
4883 run_control = normalized.get("run_control")
4884 if isinstance(run_control, dict):
4885 for key in POST_RUN_CONTROL_ALIASES["start_step"] + POST_RUN_CONTROL_ALIASES["end_step"]:
4886 run_control.pop(key, None)
4887 # Reducers read the recipe's outputs without changing them, so adding or revising
4888 # one must not move the recipe to a new home and recompute every field.
4889 normalized.pop("reducers", None)
4890 digest = hashlib.sha256(
4891 json.dumps(normalized, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
4892 ).hexdigest()[:12]
4893 return f"{label}-{digest}"

5107def resolve_run_lineage(run_dir: str, scope: str = "lineage") -> list:
5108 """!
5109 @brief Return root-to-leaf run segments, for a ParaView collection or a reducer's metrics.
5110 @param[in] run_dir Leaf run whose lineage is resolved.
5111 @param[in] scope Either run-local or full-lineage collection scope.
5112 @return Ordered run-segment mappings from root to leaf.
5113 @details Each entry carries the run path, manifest, and the checkpoint at which
5114 that run branched from its parent. Cycles and unresolved parents fail.
5115 """
5116 current = os.path.abspath(run_dir)
5117 reverse = []
5118 seen_ids = set()
5119 while True:
5120 manifest = _read_json_if_exists(os.path.join(current, "manifest.json")) or {}
5121 run_id = manifest.get("run_id") or os.path.basename(current)
5122 if run_id in seen_ids:
5123 chain = " -> ".join([entry["run_id"] for entry in reversed(reverse)] + [run_id])
5124 raise ValueError(f"Cycle detected while resolving visualization lineage: {chain}")
5125 seen_ids.add(run_id)
5126 lineage = manifest.get("lineage") or {"relationship": "root"}
5127 reverse.append({
5128 "run_dir": current,
5129 "run_id": run_id,
5130 "manifest": manifest,
5131 "lineage": lineage,
5132 "fork_step": (int(lineage["checkpoint_step"])
5133 if lineage.get("relationship") == "branch" else None),
5134 })
5135 if scope == "run" or lineage.get("relationship") != "branch":
5136 break
5137 current = _resolve_lineage_parent_run(current, lineage)
5138 return list(reversed(reverse))

5165def _checkpoint_time_for_series(run_dir: str, step: int, fallback: dict, time_scale: float = 1.0) -> float:
5166 """!
5167 @brief Read the authoritative time of one visualization frame.
5168 @details Checkpoints record solver time. A dimensionalized recipe writes physical
5169 frames, so its collection reports physical time: the checkpoint time
5170 multiplied by the owning run's reference time.
5171 @param[in] run_dir Run owning the frame.
5172 @param[in] step Frame checkpoint step.
5173 @param[in] fallback Existing collection times, already in the collection's units,
5174 used after checkpoint pruning.
5175 @param[in] time_scale Factor from solver time to the collection's time unit.
5176 @return Frame time in the collection's unit system.
5177 """
5178 metadata_path = os.path.join(
5179 run_dir, CANONICAL_RUN_PATHS["checkpoints"],
5180 f"step_{step:0{CHECKPOINT_STEP_WIDTH}d}", "checkpoint.meta",
5181 )
5182 commit_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(metadata_path), "COMMITTED")
5183 if os.path.isfile(metadata_path) and os.path.isfile(commit_path):
5184 options = _read_checkpoint_options(metadata_path)
5185 try:
5186 recorded_step = int(options["checkpoint_step"])
5187 physical_time = float(options["checkpoint_time"])
5188 except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
5189 raise ValueError(f"Checkpoint time metadata is malformed: {metadata_path}") from exc
5190 if recorded_step != step or not math.isfinite(physical_time):
5191 raise ValueError(f"Checkpoint time metadata does not match step {step}: {metadata_path}")
5192 return physical_time * time_scale
5193 if step in fallback:
5194 return float(fallback[step])
5195 raise ValueError(
5196 f"Visualization frame at step {step} has no locally available checkpoint time in "
5197 f"'{run_dir}'. Restore its checkpoints or retain an existing PVD carrying the time."
5198 )

5277 if _post_requests_particle_output(post_cfg):
5278 families.append(("particle", io_cfg.get("particle_filename_prefix", "Particle"), "vtp"))

5294 return 1.0
5295 case_path = os.path.join(segment["run_dir"], "config", "case.yml")
5296 return reference_scale(TIME, resolve_reference_scales(read_yaml_file(case_path)))

5304 if segment["fork_step"] is not None:
5305 lower = max(lower, int(segment["fork_step"]))
5306 upper = requested_end

5313 )

5322 found.append((int(match.group(1)), os.path.join(viz_dir, name)))
5323 if not found and index + 1 < len(active_segments):
5324 raise ValueError(
5325 f"Lineage run '{segment['run_id']}' has no {prefix} visualization "
5326 f"frames for its required segment {lower}..{upper} and recipe '{recipe_id}'."
5327 )
5328 for step, frame_path in sorted(found):
5329 entries.append({
5330 "step": step,
5331 "time": _checkpoint_time_for_series(segment["run_dir"], step, fallback,
5332 segment_time_scale(segment)),

5339 if current["time"] <= previous["time"]:
5340 raise ValueError(
5341 f"ParaView series time is not strictly increasing: {previous['run_id']} "
5342 f"step {previous['step']} has {previous['time']:.17g}, followed by "
5343 f"{current['run_id']} step {current['step']} at {current['time']:.17g}."
5344 )

5619def post_step_outputs(run_dir: str, post_cfg: dict, monitor_cfg=None):
5620 """!
5621 @brief Return a lookup of the output files one step of the current recipe holds.
5622 @details A step is complete when every family it must produce has its output. The
5623 post-processor writes a statistics window's output at a step only if the
5624 window had accumulated a sample in the bundle it reads, the pinned
5625 source_step or the step itself, so a window that had not opened yet is not
5626 required there.
5627 @param[in] run_dir Run whose output is inspected.
5628 @param[in] post_cfg Runtime recipe with canonical paths.
5629 @param[in] monitor_cfg Parsed monitor configuration.
5630 @return Function mapping a step to (per-step files, shared files), or None when the
5631 step lacks an output it must have.
5632 """
5633 families = collect_post_completion_families(run_dir, post_cfg, monitor_cfg)
5634 pinned = normalize_post_field_statistics_config(post_cfg).get("source_step")
5635 sample_cache = {}
5636
5637 def expected(window, step):
5638 """!
5639 @brief Whether a family's output must exist at this step.
5640 @param[in] window Field-statistics window the family belongs to, or None.
5641 @param[in] step Processed step.
5642 @return True when the family is always required or its window had samples.
5643 """
5644 if window is None:
5645 return True
5646 source = int(pinned) if pinned is not None else step
5647 if source not in sample_cache:
5648 sample_cache[source] = _field_statistics_window_samples(run_dir, source)
5649 samples = sample_cache[source]
5650 # Without the checkpoint's record the output cannot be ruled out, so it stays required.
5651 return samples is None or samples.get(window, 0) > 0

5655 @brief Collect one step's output files.
5656 @param[in] step Processed step.
5657 @return (per-step files, shared files), or None when an expected output is missing.
5658 """
5659 own, shared = [], []
5660 for mapping, window, per_step in families:
5661 if step in mapping:
5662 (own if per_step else shared).append(mapping[step])
5663 elif expected(window, step):
5664 return None
5665 return own, shared
5666
5667 return outputs

5727 """!
5728 @brief Detect the highest contiguous fully available source step for live post-processing.
5729 @param[in] source_dir Argument passed to `detect_post_source_frontier()`.
5730 @param[in] monitor_cfg Argument passed to `detect_post_source_frontier()`.
5731 @param[in] post_cfg Argument passed to `detect_post_source_frontier()`.
5732 @param[in] start_step Argument passed to `detect_post_source_frontier()`.
5733 @param[in] end_step Argument passed to `detect_post_source_frontier()`.
5734 @param[in] step_interval Argument passed to `detect_post_source_frontier()`.
5735 @return Value returned by `detect_post_source_frontier()`.
5736 """

5738 'first_requested_step': start_step,
5739 'first_incomplete_step': None,
5740 'missing_files_for_first_incomplete_step': [],
5741 'closest_complete_step_to_start': None,
5742 'closest_complete_step_to_end': None,
5743 }
5744 if step_interval <= 0 or end_step < start_step or not os.path.isdir(source_dir):
5745 return {
5746 'frontier_step': None,
5747 'diagnostic': diagnostic,
5748 }

5751 diagnostic['closest_complete_step_to_start'] = _nearest_step(complete_steps, start_step)
5752 diagnostic['closest_complete_step_to_end'] = _nearest_step(complete_steps, end_step)
5753

5755 for step in _iter_post_steps(start_step, end_step, step_interval):
5756 try:
5757 validate_committed_checkpoint(
5758 source_dir, step,
5759 require_particles=source_scan.get('require_particles', False),
5760 )
5761 except CheckpointIndexWidthError:
5762 raise
5763 except ValueError:
5764 expected_paths = _expected_source_paths_for_step(step, source_scan, post_cfg)

5766 diagnostic['missing_files_for_first_incomplete_step'] = [
5767 os.path.relpath(path, source_dir) for path in expected_paths if not os.path.isfile(path)
5768 ]
5769 if not diagnostic['missing_files_for_first_incomplete_step']:
5770 diagnostic['missing_files_for_first_incomplete_step'] = [
5771 os.path.relpath(_checkpoint_bundle_path(source_dir, step), source_dir)
5772 + ' (invalid bundle)'
5773 ]
5774 break
5775 frontier = step

Decide whether one step's existing output is still valid.

Output stays valid while it was made by the same recipe from the checkpoint now on disk. The build that made it does not invalidate it: a rebuild changes every binary's hash, and redoing a whole window after each one is what --recompute is for. Output without a record (written before records existed, or by a job killed before it could record) is accepted when it is newer than its checkpoint, or when the checkpoint is no longer local.

Parameters

[in]commitCheckpoint identity from _checkpoint_commit(), or None.
[in]recipeCurrent recipe fingerprint.
[in]recomputeWhether the invocation regenerates every step.
Returns
None when the output is valid, else the reason it must be (re)made: missing, recompute, recipe, or checkpoint.

5840def classify_post_step(record, files, commit, recipe: str, recompute: bool = False) -> "str | None":
5841 """!
5842 @brief Decide whether one step's existing output is still valid.
5843 @details Output stays valid while it was made by the same recipe from the checkpoint
5844 now on disk. The build that made it does not invalidate it: a rebuild changes
5845 every binary's hash, and redoing a whole window after each one is what
5846 `--recompute` is for. Output without a record (written before records
5847 existed, or by a job killed before it could record) is accepted when it is
5848 newer than its checkpoint, or when the checkpoint is no longer local.
5849 @param[in] record The step's record, or None.
5850 @param[in] files Files the step's output consists of, or None when any is missing.
5851 @param[in] commit Checkpoint identity from _checkpoint_commit(), or None.
5852 @param[in] recipe Current recipe fingerprint.
5853 @param[in] recompute Whether the invocation regenerates every step.
5854 @return None when the output is valid, else the reason it must be (re)made:
5855 `missing`, `recompute`, `recipe`, or `checkpoint`.
5856 """
5857 if files is None or (not files and record is None):
5858 return "missing"
5859 if recompute:
5860 return "recompute"
5861 if record is None:
5862 if commit is None or min(os.path.getmtime(path) for path in files) >= commit[1]:
5863 return None
5864 return "checkpoint"
5865 if record.get("recipe") != recipe:
5866 return "recipe"
5867 if commit is not None and record.get("checkpoint") not in (None, commit[0]):
5868 return "checkpoint"
5869 return None

5873 """!
5874 @brief Warn when another recipe in this run already produced outputs this one repeats.
5875 @details A recipe writes one file per step holding all its fields, so a recipe that
5876 repeats another's fields recomputes them rather than reusing them. The
5877 warning names the shared fields and statistics windows and the overlapping
5878 steps, so the new outputs can go into a recipe of their own instead.

5909 (other_cfg.get('io') or {}).get('output_filename_prefix', 'Field'))

6368 interrupted job completed are kept. A step is credited only when all its

6371 @param[in] post_recipe_path The recipe the job was staged with.

6378 list_path = get_post_step_list_path(run_dir, post_cfg)

6406 for path in (list_path, list_path + ".json"):

6408 os.remove(path)
6409 print(f"[INFO] Post job recorded {len(records)} of {len(job['outputs_before'])} planned step(s).")

6472def compute_physical_case_identity(case_cfg: dict) -> str:
6473 """!
6474 @brief Compute the hidden identity used to guard in-place continuation.
6475 @details Run length/timestep controls, the MPI domain decomposition, and particle
6476 load-vs-init policy do not define the physical case. All other case.yml
6477 content does. Checkpoints are decomposition-independent, so a run may
6478 continue on a different rank layout.

6483 if isinstance(normalized, dict):
6484 normalized.pop("run_control", None)
6485 grid = normalized.get("grid")
6486 if isinstance(grid, dict):
6487 for key in GRID_DA_PROCESSOR_KEYS:
6488 grid.pop(key, None)
6489 if isinstance(grid.get("programmatic_settings"), dict):
6490 for key in GRID_DA_PROCESSOR_KEYS:
6491 grid["programmatic_settings"].pop(key, None)
6492 particles = (((normalized.get("models") or {}).get("physics") or {}).get("particles"))
6493 if isinstance(particles, dict):
6494 particles.pop("restart_mode", None)
6495 payload = json.dumps(
6496 normalized, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False
6497 ).encode("utf-8")

6699 lock = read_yaml_file(str(candidate / "inputs" / "assets.lock.yml")) \

6703 if current_grid:

6707 elif isinstance(runtime_grid, dict):

6714 except CheckpointIndexWidthError:

6719 candidates.append((ordering, candidate.stat().st_mtime_ns, str(candidate)))

6723 "Restore a run from storage first, or name one explicitly with --from <run-dir>."

7096def validate_and_nondimensionalize_picgrid(source_grid: str, dest_grid: str, L_ref: float, expected_nblk: int = None) -> dict:
7097 """!
7098 @brief Validates PICGRID payload and writes a non-dimensionalized copy.
7099 @details Streams the rows, so the grid is never held in memory; `picgrid.py` owns the format.
7100 @param[in] source_grid Input grid file path.
7101 @param[in] dest_grid Output grid file path.
7102 @param[in] L_ref Reference length for non-dimensionalization.
7103 @param[in] expected_nblk Optional expected block count.
7104 @return Summary dictionary with nblk, dims, and total_nodes.
7105 @throws ValueError on malformed grid.
7106 """
7107 picgrid = load_shared_module("picgrid")
7108 if L_ref == 0.0:
7109 raise ValueError("length_ref must be non-zero when processing grid coordinates.")
7110 if not os.path.isfile(source_grid):
7111 raise ValueError(f"Grid file not found: {source_grid}")
7112
7113 with open(source_grid, "r") as fin:
7114 line_iter = picgrid.content_lines(fin)
7115 dims = picgrid.read_picgrid_header(line_iter, source_grid, expected_nblk)
7116 nblk = len(dims)
7117
7118 total_nodes_expected = sum(im * jm * km for (im, jm, km) in dims)
7119 os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(dest_grid), exist_ok=True)
7120 with open(dest_grid, "w") as fout:
7121 fout.write("PICGRID\n")
7122 fout.write(f"{nblk}\n")
7123 for (im, jm, km) in dims:
7124 fout.write(f"{im} {jm} {km}\n")
7125
7126 total_nodes_seen = 0
7127 for lineno, coord_line in line_iter:
7128 point = picgrid.parse_coordinate_row(lineno, coord_line, source_grid)
7129 total_nodes_seen += 1
7130 if total_nodes_seen > total_nodes_expected:
7131 raise ValueError(
7132 f"Grid file '{source_grid}' has more coordinates ({total_nodes_seen}) than expected ({total_nodes_expected})."
7133 )
7134 fout.write(" ".join(picgrid.format_picgrid_coordinate(value / L_ref) for value in point) + "\n")
7135
7136 if total_nodes_seen != total_nodes_expected:
7137 raise ValueError(
7138 f"Grid file '{source_grid}' has {total_nodes_seen} coordinates, expected {total_nodes_expected} from header."
7139 )
7140
7141 return {"nblk": nblk, "dims": dims, "total_nodes": total_nodes_expected}

7580def _resolve_case_relative_path(path_value: str, case_dir: str) -> str:
7581 """!
7582 @brief Resolve a path relative to the current case directory.
7583 @param[in] path_value Path from case.yml.
7584 @param[in] case_dir Current case directory.
7585 @return Absolute path.
7586 """
7587 if not isinstance(path_value, str) or not path_value.strip():
7588 raise ValueError("path value must be a non-empty string.")
7589 workspace_root = find_workspace_root(case_dir)
7590 if workspace_root:
7591 if os.path.isabs(path_value):
7592 raise ValueError(
7593 f"absolute path {path_value!r} is not allowed in workspace case configuration; "
7594 "use 'picurv inputs import --mode reference' for an explicit external reference."
7595 )
7596 resolved = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(workspace_root, path_value))
7597 if os.path.commonpath([workspace_root, resolved]) != os.path.abspath(workspace_root):
7598 raise ValueError(f"path {path_value!r} escapes the workspace.")
7599 if resolved.endswith(".reference.yml") and os.path.isfile(resolved):
7600 pointer = read_yaml_file(resolved)
7601 external = pointer.get("picurv_external_reference") if isinstance(pointer, dict) else None
7602 if not isinstance(external, str) or not os.path.isabs(external):
7603 raise ValueError(f"Invalid external-reference descriptor: {resolved}")
7604 if not os.path.isfile(external):
7605 raise ValueError(f"Registered external input is unavailable: {external}")
7606 return external
7607 return resolved
7608 if os.path.isabs(path_value):
7609 return os.path.abspath(path_value)
7610 return os.path.abspath(os.path.join(case_dir, path_value))

7734def validate_grid_generator_cli_args(cli_args, case_path: str) -> list:
7735 """!
7736 @brief Check closed-choice values inside the generator's opaque token list.
7737 @details `cli_args` is passed through to grid.gen untouched, so a misspelled geometry
7738 selector there is only discovered when the subprocess exits nonzero partway
7739 into a run. The generator remains the authority; this reports the same set
7740 earlier, and stays silent on anything it does not recognize.
7741 @param[in] cli_args Raw token list from grid.generator.cli_args.
7742 @param[in] case_path Case file path for diagnostics.
7743 @return List of error strings.
7744 """
7745 if not isinstance(cli_args, list):
7746 return []
7747 tokens = [str(token) for token in cli_args]
7748 errors = []
7749 for index, token in enumerate(tokens):
7750 values = []
7751 for follower in tokens[index + 1:]:
7752 if follower.startswith("--"):
7753 break
7754 values.append(follower)
7755 if token in GRID_GENERATOR_CHOICE_FLAGS:
7756 allowed = GRID_GENERATOR_CHOICE_FLAGS[token]
7757 for value in values[:1]:
7758 if value not in allowed:
7759 errors.append(
7760 f" {case_path}: grid.generator.cli_args {token} must be one of "
7761 f"{list(allowed)} (got '{value}')."
7762 )
7763 elif token in GRID_GENERATOR_SPEC_FLAGS:
7764 allowed = GRID_GENERATOR_SPEC_FLAGS[token]
7765 for value in values:
7766 kind = value.split(":", 1)[0]
7767 if kind not in allowed:
7768 errors.append(
7769 f" {case_path}: grid.generator.cli_args {token} entry '{value}' "
7770 f"names '{kind}', which is not one of {list(allowed)}."
7771 )
7772 return errors

8039 @brief The profile data sources named by a case's unprepared prescribed_velocity inlets.
8040 @details A source given by name resolves to its shared mapping under `sources:`, so

8042 resolve_velocity_source() resolves them; nothing here raises, validation does.

8048 """!
8049 @brief The data terms of one source, its sum terms searched in turn.
8050 @param[in] spec Source as written.

8052 @param[in] visiting Names being expanded on this path, so a cycle ends the search.
8053 @return Data-term mappings.

8210 @brief Normalize boundary_conditions to list-of-lists form: one list of face entries per block.
8211 @details A single face list, one whose first entry is a mapping, is block 0's. Given
8212 `num_blocks`, the layout is validated: an empty section, a single list for a
8213 multi-block case, or another block count raises. Without it the reading is lenient,
8214 for code that inspects a case before validation reports its errors: anything but a
8215 non-empty list is no blocks, and a block that is not a list has no entries.
8216 @param[in] all_blocks_bcs The `boundary_conditions` value as written.
8217 @param[in] num_blocks Declared block count, or None for the lenient reading.
8218 @return The list of blocks; validated, it is the input itself when that was already one.
8219 """

8221 if not isinstance(all_blocks_bcs, list) or not all_blocks_bcs:
8222 return []
8223 if isinstance(all_blocks_bcs[0], dict):
8224 return [all_blocks_bcs]

8228

8240 f"Mismatch: case.yml declares {num_blocks} block(s) but found {len(all_blocks_bcs)} BC definitions."

8331def _case_reynolds_number(case_cfg: dict):
8332 """!
8333 @brief Reynolds number implied by a case's scaling and fluid properties.
8334 @param[in] case_cfg Parsed case configuration.
8335 @return The Reynolds number, or None when the inputs are absent or unusable.
8336 """
8337 try:
8338 props = case_cfg.get('properties', {}) or {}
8339 scaling = props.get('scaling', {}) or {}
8340 fluid = props.get('fluid', {}) or {}
8341 density = float(fluid.get('density'))
8342 viscosity = float(fluid.get('viscosity'))
8343 length_ref = float(scaling.get('length_ref'))
8344 velocity_ref = float(scaling.get('velocity_ref'))
8345 except (TypeError, ValueError):
8346 return None
8347 if viscosity <= 0.0:
8348 return None
8349 return density * velocity_ref * length_ref / viscosity

8760def _lookup_allowed_schema_keys(schema: dict, path: tuple):
8761 """!
8762 @brief Return allowed keys for a path, honoring '*' dynamic mapping entries.
8763 @param[in] schema Role schema mapping.
8764 @param[in] path Internal path tuple.
8765 @return Allowed key set, None for free-form mappings, or False when path is not schema-checked.
8766 """
8767 if path in schema:
8768 return schema[path]
8769 for idx, part in enumerate(path):
8770 if part == "[]":
8771 continue
8772 candidate = path[:idx] + ("*",) + path[idx + 1:]
8773 if candidate in schema:
8774 return schema[candidate]
8775 return False

8806def _validate_yaml_schema_keys(cfg, schema: dict, file_path: str, errors: list, path: tuple = ()) -> None:
8807 """!
8808 @brief Reject unsupported YAML keys before they can be silently ignored by staging.
8809 @param[in] cfg Parsed YAML node.
8810 @param[in] schema Role schema mapping.
8811 @param[in] file_path Source file path for diagnostics.
8812 @param[in,out] errors Validation error accumulator.
8813 @param[in] path Current internal YAML path tuple.
8814 """
8815 if isinstance(cfg, dict):
8816 allowed = _lookup_allowed_schema_keys(schema, path)
8817 if allowed is not False and allowed is not None:
8818 unknown = sorted(str(key) for key in cfg.keys() if key not in allowed)
8819 for key in unknown:
8820 hint = _schema_key_hint(schema, path, key, allowed)
8821 hint_text = f" {hint}" if hint else ""
8822 errors.append(
8823 f" {file_path}: unsupported key at {_schema_path_text(path)}: '{key}'. "
8824 f"Allowed keys: {sorted(allowed)}.{hint_text}"
8825 )
8826 if allowed is None:
8827 return
8828 for key, value in cfg.items():
8829 _validate_yaml_schema_keys(value, schema, file_path, errors, path + (key,))
8830 elif isinstance(cfg, list) and _lookup_allowed_schema_keys(schema, path + ("[]",)) is not False:
8831 for item in cfg:
8832 _validate_yaml_schema_keys(item, schema, file_path, errors, path + ("[]",))
8833 elif (isinstance(cfg, (str, int, float, list)) and not isinstance(cfg, bool)
8834 and path and path[-1] != "[]" and _lookup_allowed_schema_keys(schema, path) is not False):
8835 # A section given as a string, number or list would reach code that reads it as a
8836 # mapping. A boolean is left alone: several sections take true/false as shorthand
8837 # (models.physics.turbulence.les, io.paraview_series). So are list items, some of
8838 # which accept a scalar shorthand (a study metric name).
8839 errors.append(
8840 f" {file_path}: '{_schema_path_text(path)}' must be a mapping, not "
8841 f"{type(cfg).__name__} {cfg!r}."
8842 )
8843 elif isinstance(cfg, list):
8844 for item in cfg:
8845 _validate_yaml_schema_keys(item, schema, file_path, errors, path + ("[]",))
8846
